published_verifier.scope: Retrospective policy-v3 verifier only; future live inputs require matching preparation.

maintenance: Three assertion parameters plus explicit subset documentation and profile v3. Reused the existing verifier image, artifact downloader, isolated grading worker, bounded Docker diagnostics and retrospective workflow. Added focused Boolean controls and a verifier-only observer of native per-variant results; scorer, reference, mutants, test entry point and isolation are unchanged. No new cache, service or Harbor override.
limitations: The policy correction followed inspection of both outputs and is not a prospectively frozen validation.
One pair on one case cannot establish that the skill is effective or ineffective, or justify Harbor adoption.
File-access attempts do not prove successful reads, instruction following or causal benefit.
Only the declared bounded assertion subset is qualified; documented unsupported Pester forms remain outside coverage.
Clarified documentation is a changed future input; these agents received the original version-two documentation. Future live use requires matching agent inputs and manifests; none were rebuilt.
conclusion: Both unchanged submissions pass the reference and detect both defects under one corrected isolated verifier. No quality advantage was observed on this case. The current suite runs 32 tests and absent 35; that count difference is not a measured quality advantage. This is a usable retrospective comparison, not evidence that the skill is ineffective or that Harbor adoption is justified.
next_step: Freeze the qualified assertion subset and controls before selecting one held-out case with more opportunity to distinguish test quality. Predeclare the comparison metrics and use matched inputs under separate authorization. Do not revise the skill until a repeated, concrete weakness supports a targeted change.
